originality.rationale: The originating 2026 paper defines the finite-round map and gives linear invasion and numerical one-stage stabilization, but not all-parameter prime-two nonexistence, all-parameter endemic Schur stability, or a monotonicity sharpness witness. The 2021 discrete SIR recurrence differs in infection/turnover accounting and has only a parameter-restricted global endemic stability theorem; the 2014 Euler-incidence model admits period-doubling because it is a distinct update, and cannot cover the bounded competing-risk family. Accessible own claims concern local threshold behavior or stochastic branching for the same source, not the global two-cycle obstruction. Searches cannot rule out unindexed general sign theorems.
residual_risks: General planar competitive-map or nonlinear-incidence no-two-cycle theorems predating 2026 may imply this special case without model-identifying terms; bounded literature searches cannot certify absolute novelty.

value.rationale: The source contrasts numerical one-stage stabilization with two-stage chaos but lacks an all-step-size proof. A universal period-two obstruction, strict all-rate endemic Schur stability, and a smooth probability-preserving counterexample when monotonicity is removed expose the exact mechanism preventing period-doubling in the physically derived one-stage map. This is a motivated structural result, not a numerical threshold increment or a restatement of the known invasion formula.
